00363|   // what the M = 1 pair reads. (Spec 8: skipped when step_mtp_kv already wrote it.)

00367|                 at(s.resid, size_t(last_row) * s.desc().hidden * 2),
00368|                 at(s.x, size_t(last_row) * s.desc().hidden * 2), 1u);
00369| 
00370|   // lm_head at M = 1 through the EXISTING decode binary, chosen off the loaded
00371|   // weight's kind exactly as capture.cc:625-631 chooses it. It writes straight
00372|   // into `logits`: `gemv.cl`'s `out[(s*M + m)*N + n]` at S = 1, M = 1 IS the
00373|   // [1][N] row `argmax_stage1` reads. **Not `dequant_to_bf16` + `gemm_bf16`**:
00374|   // the lm_head's [5120][248320] bf16 expansion is 2.54 GB, seven times the
00375|   // dequant scratch, for one row of output.

00381|               lm.shape.N / 64, lm.shape.S, 1,

00436| void step_mtp_kv(Context& cx, KernelCache& kc, PrefillScratch& s, const LoadedModel& m,
00437|                  void* hctl, uint32_t pos, uint32_t C, uint16_t* hid, const KvLayer& kv) {
00438|   require(m.mtp != nullptr, "step_mtp_kv without the MTP head");
00439|   // Spec 15e: a MoE head (Ornith's) fills its KV through this same front - fc, the input
00440|   // norm, q||k||v, attn_prep; its MoE FFN never runs in prefill. The only MoE term is the
00441|   // final norm's fold below (nothing to fold after a MoE block, as step_head's).

00444|   const uint32_t H = m.desc->hidden, G = PrefillScratch::kNormGroups;
00445|   // q||gate is [0, q_proj) and k||v [q_proj, qkv) (Qwen3.8 12288 / 14336); the
00446|   // slab walk below starts at q_proj, a whole number of 1024-column slabs.
00447|   const uint32_t kv_n0 = m.desc->fa_q_proj_n();
00448|   require(kv_n0 % kernels::kPfSlabWidth == 0, "q_proj is not a whole number of slabs");
00449|   // 1. The main model's final norm on every row (what decode's b.x holds after a
00450|   //    step), into hid rows 1..C. step_head's own single-row norm is then skipped.

00452|               s.partials.ptr(), s.resid.ptr(), hid + H, C);
00453|   const uint32_t rows = mtp_kv_rows(pos, C);

00455|   const uint32_t r0 = C - rows;   // 1 at pos 0 (no h_{-1}), else 0
00456|   // 2. embed(ids[r0 + r]) -> resid rows (the main residual is dead after step 1).
00457|   cx.launch(kc(kernels::pf_embed_gather_variant(s.desc().hidden), "pf_embed_gather"), 1, rows, 1,
00458|             {PtrArg(s.ids.as<uint32_t>() + r0), PtrArg(m.embed.ptr()), PtrArg(s.resid.ptr()),
00459|              arg_val(rows)});
00460|   // 3. The two pre-fc norms into one [rows][2 x hidden] row of x: embed first, hidden second.
00461|   const std::string fold0 = kernels::pf_res_fold_variant(H, 0, G);
00462|   const std::string cat = kernels::pf_norm_finish_strided_variant(H, G, G, 2 * H);
00463|   auto fold_norm = [&](const std::string& fv, const std::string& nv, const void* partials,

00720| // cos/sin[p][0..1][i] for the 64 rotary dims (partial_rotary_factor 0.25 of
00721| // head_dim 256), i < 32. Text-mode interleaved mRoPE copies one position id
00722| // onto every frequency stream, so this is plain RoPE (docs/03 "Layer math").
00723| std::vector<float> rope_table(uint32_t max_len) {
00724|   const uint32_t half = Qwen35::kRotaryDim / 2;
00725|   std::vector<float> t(size_t(max_len) * 2 * half);
00726|   std::vector<double> inv(half);
00727|   for (uint32_t i = 0; i < half; ++i)
00728|     inv[i] = std::pow(Qwen35::kRopeTheta, -2.0 * double(i) / double(Qwen35::kRotaryDim));
00729|   for (uint32_t p = 0; p < max_len; ++p)
00730|     for (uint32_t i = 0; i < half; ++i) {
00731|       const double a = double(p) * inv[i];
00732|       t[(size_t(p) * 2 + 0) * half + i] = float(std::cos(a));
00733|       t[(size_t(p) * 2 + 1) * half + i] = float(std::sin(a));
